items.title: [Frontend] [Parser] Migrate llama3_json/llama4_json to the streaming parser engine
items.body:
# Purpose `llama3_json` streaming and non-streaming disagree: the legacy parser re-parses a cumulative buffer with fixed separator arithmetic, so at more than one token per SSE delta it returns tool calls that do not parse — **174/858 valid at 5 tokens/delta (20.3%), against 858/858 here**. This migrates `Llama3JsonToolParser` (registry names `llama3_json`, `llama4_json`) onto the declarative `ParserEngine`, where non-streaming replays the same state machine as streaming, so the two agree by construction. It also un-breaks `llama4_json`, which raised at construction on real Llama-4 tokenizers. | tokens per SSE delta | legacy, valid JSON | legacy, AST-correct | this branch, valid JSON | this branch, AST-correct | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 849/858 (99.0%) | 379/858 (44.2%) | **858/858 (100.0%)** | **672/858 (78.3%)** | | 2 | 405/858 (47.2%) | 166/858 (19.3%) | **858/858 (100.0%)** | **672/858 (78.3%)** | | 5 | 174/858 (20.3%) | 62/858 (7.2%) | **858/858 (100.0%)** | **672/858 (78.3%)** | Measured live, **streaming**, on the full BFCL v4 set (858 cases, `simple_python`/`live_simple`/`multiple`): each parser's exact generated tokens replayed through `extract_tool_calls_streaming` at 1/2/5 tokens/delta, scored with `bfcl-eval`'s own `ast_checker`. This branch is flat across every chunk size — not just "still valid JSON" but "still the right call" — matching the 78.1% non-streaming weighted accuracy in the eval section below.
Reproducing the headline table ```bash pip install "bfcl-eval>=2025.10.20.1,<2026" vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --max-model-len 8192 \ --served-model-name localmodel --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser llama3_json .venv/bin/python bfcl_stream_replay.py ``` Download [bfcl_stream_replay.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33303165/bfcl_stream_replay.py) To score legacy the same way: swap the checkout (unmodified `main`), run with **that checkout's own `.venv/bin/python`**, and add `--tool-call-parser legacy_llama3_json`.
Model eval — official bfcl-eval, live, n=858 Ran `bfcl-eval==2025.12.17.1` directly against two separate live `vllm serve` instances, **non-streaming** (`bfcl-eval` does one-shot generation), same model, greedy decoding, same 858 BFCL **v4** test cases — `simple_python`, `live_simple`, `multiple`, the full category files the package ships, not a subsample: this branch with `--tool-call-parser llama3_json` on one GPU, and the real pre-migration `Llama3JsonToolParser` — an unmodified current-`main` checkout, where the registry still resolves `llama3_json` to the legacy class — on a second GPU. | category | n | legacy (pre-migration) | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | non-live simple (Python) | 400 | 41.50% | **83.00%** | | non-live multiple | 200 | 32.00% | **80.50%** | | live simple | 258 | 52.33% | **68.60%** | | weighted average | 858 | 42.5% | **78.1%** | **Reproducing this table:** ```bash pip install "bfcl-eval>=2025.10.20.1,<2026" vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --max-model-len 8192 \ --served-model-name localmodel --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser llama3_json .venv/bin/python bfcl_nonstream.py ``` Download [bfcl_nonstream.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33303180/bfcl_nonstream.py) Expect the per-category accuracies above (± minor model/hardware noise); Scores land in `./score/data_non_live.csv` and `./score/data_live.csv`. Swap the checkout (unmodified `main`, where the registry still resolves `llama3_json` to the legacy class) to score the legacy parser the same way — no flag change needed.
*AI assistance was used in preparing this change (Claude Code): adversarial review, rebase analysis and test-harness work. I have reviewed every changed line and run every test reported below.* **Scope: 14 files, `+4837/-380`** (`+1837/-380` excluding tests). `llama_json.py` itself is **779 lines** — down from an earlier 1532/1438, after moving the generic resumable/truncated-JSON scanning and schema-coercion-safety splicing out to `vllm/parser/json_scan.py`, `vllm/parser/utils.py`, and `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py`, where the same machinery is available to every parser, not just this one. **No behaviour changes for any other parser** — the `engine/` files touched register this parser's adapter and gain a config flag (`tool_call_ends_on_args_balance`) that defaults to `False` and whose only setter is `llama_json.py`.
Design The LLama JSON format is a bare envelope with no wrapper and no end marker: ``` [<|python_tag|>]{"name": "f", "parameters": {...}}; {"name": "g", ...} ``` Most tool-call formats tell the engine where a call starts and ends for free. Qwen3 wraps a call in `...`. Granite has no closing token, but `` still marks the start, and the body is one JSON array the engine already knows how to split. Llama's `<|python_tag|>` is optional, and when present isn't always followed by JSON — the model can put ordinary ipython-style text after it — so it isn't trusted as an opener the way Granite's marker is; the engine just consumes it as text and waits to see what actually follows. `{` ends up doing the opener's job instead: it's both the opener and ordinary text (prose can contain one too), and the call ends only when the JSON balances. Llama's bare envelope doesn't match an existing engine mode, so this parser answers four questions those other formats get for free: - **When does tool call ends** When the JSON balances - a new engine flag `tool_call_ends_on_args_balance` rather than a closing terminal, so separators (`;`, a newline) don't matter. - **What's the tool name, and what are its arguments** The envelope's top level `"name"` key (not one nested in the arguments), `arguments/parameters` are the model's own text, not a rebuilt JSON object - so the client sees exactly what the model wrote. - **What if the model never finishes the JSON** Cut back to the longest prefix that's still valid and closed by appending - never by rewriting text already streamed. - **What if it looks like a call but it isn't** A balanced `{...}` with no top-level `"name"` key is prose. Its events are retracted and the text restored as content. Implementation notes: - Separators `;`, newlines, commas, a second `<|python_tag|>`, or nothing at all (the xgrammar `llama` structural tag for `tool_choice="required"` forces back-to-back `{...}{...}`) all work, since the parser isn't looking for one. - The top-level `"name"` lookup is a structural scan, not the engine's regex fallback, which would match a `"name"` nested inside `parameters`. - A prose `{...}` that gets retracted has its slot recycled, so real calls still stream with dense indices from 0. - `tool_choice="required"` and named choice are handled by this parser directly (`supports_required_and_named = False`), as the other engine parsers do. - `llama_tool_parser.py` is gutted in place to an adapter shim keeping the class name and `structural_tag_model="llama"`, so the registry needs no change.
Behaviour changes vs the legacy parser (9) Each is forced by streaming/non-streaming unification or is a strict improvement. Every example is measured: the same input fed to `origin/main`'s `Llama3JsonToolParser` and to this branch. `CALL` abbreviates `{"name": "f", "parameters": {"a": "x"}}`. 1. **Leading prose before a call is returned as content** (legacy: `content=None`); text after the first completed call is still dropped. ```text in Let me check. CALL legacy f({"a": "x"}) content=null new f({"a": "x"}) content="Let me check." ``` Legacy *streaming* is worse than its own non-streaming result here — it never detects the call at all: ```text legacy (streaming) no call, content = the entire string new (streaming) f({"a": "x"}) content="Let me check." ``` 2. **An envelope needs `parameters`/`arguments` next to `name` to be a call.** Name-only and prose user-data shapes stay content — unchanged from legacy, and listed because it is a refusal worth preserving. ```text in {"name": "John", "age": 30} legacy non-streaming: content = input, no call legacy streaming: a tool call named "John" with empty arguments new both: content = input, no call ``` Non-streaming this is unchanged from legacy. Streaming, legacy promotes the user's own data to a tool call — the migration removes that by construction. 3. **Valid `name` + malformed params → a call whose arguments are cut back to the longest closeable prefix**, so they always parse. See "One deliberate deviation" below. ```text in {"name": "f", "parameters": {"a": "x", bad}} legacy no call, whole string as content new f({"a": "x"}) ``` 4. **A valid call followed by a bad object no longer drops the valid call** (#49923's bug 2 — legacy was all-or-nothing). ```text in CALL I used {searchTool} here legacy no call, whole string as content new f({"a": "x"}) ``` 5. **Arguments are the verbatim model span**, not `json.dumps` re-serialisation — same JSON value, the model's own whitespace. ```text in {"name": "f", "parameters": {"a": "x"}} legacy f({"a": "x"}) new f({"a": "x"}) ``` 6. **The constructor no longer raises when `<|python_tag|>` is absent.** This un-breaks `llama4_json`, which was unusable at startup on real Llama-4 tokenizers. ```text in Llama-4 tokenizer (no <|python_tag|> in vocab) legacy RuntimeError: could not locate the bot token '<|python_tag|>' new constructs, and parses <|python_start|> ... <|python_end|> ``` 7. **Truncated mid-JSON generation emits the partial arguments, repaired to valid JSON, in both modes.** A real generation cut at `max_tokens=16`: ```text in {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"location": "Boston legacy non-streaming: no call, raw partial as content legacy streaming: get_weather({"location": "Boston"}) <- and so disagrees with itself new both: get_weather({"location": "Boston"}) ``` Legacy streaming also hands the client arguments that do not parse at all, at other truncation points — `{"query": "ll` from a real `max_tokens=20` run, and 14 of 80 cells in the workload below. 8. **Prose containing braces is preserved byte-identically in streaming too.** ```text in Code: if (x) { y(); } done legacy content = input new content = input ``` 9. **Argument values are coerced to their declared schema type, and only when the value is invalid for it.** Legacy did no coercion at all; the shared engine coerces unconditionally and so corrupts already-valid values, so this guard is what keeps it from being a regression. Largest measured difference in the eval below. ```text in {"name": "f", "parameters": {"n": "10"}} with n: integer legacy f({"n": "10"}) <- str where the schema says int new f({"n": 10}) ``` Legacy streaming additionally advanced a fixed two characters past each parsed call (`start_idx += end_idx + len("; ")`), so any separator those two characters do not cover silently dropped every call after the first (#49923's bug 1): ```text in CALL;CALL (bare ";", not "; ") legacy 1 of 2 calls new 2 of 2 calls ```
## Test Result | suite | result | | --- | --- | | `tests/parser/engine/test_llama_json.py` | **590 passed** | | `tests/parser/` | **7089 passed** | | `tests/tool_parsers/` (excl. gated-tokenizer test below) | **1184 passed**, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed | | `tests/tool_parsers/test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py` | not re-run on this exact branch (gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` tokenizer, no network/token in this environment); previously 14 passed, unaffected by a pure internal refactor | | #47562 regressions + no-reasoning-parser safety cases | **27 passed** (10 core #47562, 6 Llama serving-path marker, 11 Inkling shared-marker) | | `pre-commit` incl. `mypy` | clean |
Test Plan (commands) ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers -q \ --ignore=tests/tool_parsers/test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py \ --ignore=tests/tool_parsers/test_cohere_command_tool_parser.py .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/tool_parsers/test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files .venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy --hook-stage manual --files ``` Plus a live server on `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` for streaming/non-streaming parity, an offline `llama4_json` check against a real Llama-4 tokenizer, and a BFCL replay comparing both parsers on identical generated tokens.
On the size of the test file `tests/parser/engine/test_llama_json.py` is 2764 lines, the largest in `tests/parser/engine/`. Several things make that a budget rather than a red flag: - **`llama_json.py` itself is 779 lines**, not the 1532/1438 it was earlier in this PR's history — the generic resumable/truncated-JSON scanning (`scan_json_value`, `ValueScan`, `KeyScan`/`scan_top_level`, `closeable_prefix`, `object_members`, `array_items`, none of which reference tool calls or Llama tokens) and the verbatim-preserving schema-coercion splicer moved to `vllm/parser/json_scan.py`, `vllm/parser/utils.py`, and `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` — shared infrastructure now available to every engine parser, not bespoke complexity scoped to this file. What's left is the actual Llama-specific state machine. - **`llama_json` is excluded from the shared replay harness by design.** `test_replay.py:77` and `test_delegating_replay.py:97` skip it because a bare-JSON format has no `TOOL_END` terminal (mistral opts out for the same reason), so this file carries replay coverage the other parsers get for free. The opt-out is not silent: llama_json samples are still built and validated against the real parser at `chunk_size=1`. - **14 of its 24 classes are regression guards**, each traceable to a bug fixed on this branch or to an upstream issue (#49923, #47562, #45795).
## One deliberate deviation worth flagging Behaviour change 3 — a malformed or truncated envelope with a valid `name` is **promoted to a tool call** with its arguments cut back to the longest parseable prefix, where legacy failed closed and returned content. This follows the contract the other engine parsers already implement, and the alternative is worse: rejecting the call at close means withholding the tool name until the envelope balances, which removes incremental argument streaming for every Llama call, not just malformed ones. I have taken that as the right trade. If maintainers prefer failing closed for this parser specifically, say so and I will implement it — it is a contained change, and it is the only decision here I would expect to be contentious.
Other known limitations - **Named tool choice can return the whole envelope as the arguments** for schemas that constrain the object, when `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING=0` removes the structural tag and the model emits the envelope anyway. What prevents that is the decoding grammar, and it is backend-dependent: xgrammar rejects the envelope for a typed schema, llguidance 1.7.6 at vLLM's defaults accepts it unless `disable_additional_properties` is set. Default configuration (strict on) is unaffected. - The equivalent coercion guard for `ParserEngine._coerce_value`, which would affect the other engine parsers, is deliberately not in this PR — attempted once during the size-reduction pass and reverted when it broke gemma4's and deepseek_v32's own tests, which pin different, deliberate best-effort coercion behavior. Left as a narrowly-scoped follow-up PR with full cross-parser coverage.
Interaction with the Rust frontend vLLM ships a second `llama3_json` implementation for the Rust frontend (`rust/src/parser/src/tool/json/llama.rs`), registered for both `llama3_json` and `llama4_json`. **This PR does not touch it** — after this lands the two differ under `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND`, and no CI job compares them (the Rust Frontend Cargo job only runs on `rust/` changes). Happy to mirror the behavior there in a follow-up if maintainers want the two to agree.
Duplicate-work check Per the contributing guide; re-checked against current `main` on 2026-10-11. - #44873, the feature request this PR implements, is **closed**; no new PR has opened against this area since #51577 itself. - **#48295** and **#49923** patch the same bugs by editing the code this PR deletes — not duplicates (migration vs. targeted patch), both still **open**, and will conflict on merge since the bugs they fix become structurally impossible here. - #47562 is merged and already included through `main`. **#42210** (streaming drops content on a stop-string interrupt) is incidentally fixed for `llama3_json` by this migration but stays **open**, since it isn't fixed for the other legacy parsers.

items.title: [Kernel] Add FlashInfer GDN and KDA prefill backend selection
items.body:
## Overview

Add FlashInfer prefill selection for Qwen GDN (`auto`/`cudnn`) and all eight public KDA backends for bounded GLM/Kimi KDA, with shared state handling and versioned KDA metadata. This carries the integration from [Anerudhan/vllm#1](https://github.com/Anerudhan/vllm/pull/1); benchmark result files are excluded.

## Claims

- Add separate FlashInfer implementation selectors for GDN and KDA prefill, including `cute-dsl`, `cute-dsl-persistent`, `tirx`, `ptx`, `cake`, and `small-bh` for KDA.
- Share the KDA adapter across Kimi-K3, GLM and the bounded-gate shared Kimi path, including normalization and recurrent-state handling.
- Build contiguous int64 offsets with a tensor version counter for native KDA paths under inference mode. Omit sequence-order hints for persistent CuTe DSL, TIRx and PTX, which reject them.
- Validate hardware, dtype and gate limits. Protect borrowed state, permit updates to temporary gathered state, and reject unsupported cuDNN checkpoint and batch-invariance requests. Add CLI, metadata, state-contract and GPU replay tests.

### New arguments

| Argument | Values | Use with |
|---|---|---|
| `--flashinfer-gdn-backend` | `auto`, `cudnn` | `--gdn-prefill-backend flashinfer` |
| `--flashinfer-kda-backend` | `auto`, `cute-dsl`, `cute-dsl-persistent`, `tirx`, `ptx`, `cake`, `small-bh`, `cudnn` | `--kda-prefill-backend flashinfer` |

Both resolve to `auto` when omitted. `auto` delegates to FlashInfer's dispatcher; explicit choices retain FlashInfer's input checks. The existing provider argument must select FlashInfer to use these paths.

KDA state requirements: `auto`, `cake`, and `small-bh` use BF16; `cute-dsl` and `cudnn` accept BF16 or FP32; `cute-dsl-persistent`, `tirx`, and `ptx` require FP32. Set the existing `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` argument to match. Extra shape, GPU and dependency limits still apply. In particular, PTX requires SM103a and H64/H96. Persistent CuTe DSL, TIRx and PTX require an explicit warmed workspace for prefill graph capture; this adapter does not manage it, so use eager prefill for those choices.

```bash
# Kimi-K3: FlashInfer auto prefill with BF16 recurrent state
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --kda-prefill-backend flashinfer --flashinfer-kda-backend auto \
  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16

# Qwen GDN: explicit cuDNN prefill
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --gdn-prefill-backend flashinfer --flashinfer-gdn-backend cudnn
```

These examples show backend options; add the model's normal deployment flags.

## Validation

Current branch: changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff, mypy and test wiring, passed. `git diff --check` passed. An isolated CPU harness ran **164 checks** for backend forwarding, state dtypes, inference/strided offsets, sequence-order metadata, CLI choices and existing GDN selection contracts. The accepted KDA values match [FlashInfer main at `c0e62fa7`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c0e62fa7b18cbf051f729214984c235eb521a551/flashinfer/kda.py).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  ../artifacts/vllm-kda-backends-20261012/test_kda_backends_cpu.py -q
# 164 passed; isolated source-level harness outside the PR.
```

AWS runtime passed 74 KDA GPU tests and 44 metadata tests for the original auto/cuDNN paths. Results below retain their measured revisions and are not measurements of this backend-list update.

> **Dependency caveat:** These FlashInfer prefill paths require **FlashInfer 0.7.2**. This PR does not update vLLM's `flashinfer-python==0.7.0.post1` pin, so the serving environment must install 0.7.2 explicitly. The full backend list follows FlashInfer main at `c0e62fa7`; use a build containing the selected backend. Native CuTe DSL needs `nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.7` except for `small-bh`; TIRx needs CUDA-enabled TVM with TIRx and `tirx_kernels.tirx_lite`; PTX needs `ptxas>=13.2` and TVM FFI. The cuDNN path was validated with frontend **1.31.0** and cuDNN **9.20** on SM100/SM103. Benchmark results below retain their exact measured revisions.

### Latest microbenchmark results — GB200

Lyris job **3275022**. **B1 × 8,192-token prefill**; cells show **active CPU / GPU kernel interval union, µs/call** (lower is better), averaged over four fresh-process medians.

| Model | vLLM auto | FlashInfer auto | FlashInfer cuDNN |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kimi-K3 H6 / TP16 | 91.216 / 319.663 | 213.388 / 115.296 | 156.604 / 111.760 |
| GLM-5.3 H16 / TP4 | 163.516 / 457.645 | 285.176 / 340.012 | 158.200 / 184.161 |
| QwenNext Q8/V16 / TP2 | 259.956 / 118.064 | 265.132 / 117.528 | 219.848 / 129.161 |
| Qwen3.5 Q16/V32 / TP1 | 272.872 / 179.055 | 277.384 / 179.354 | 230.468 / 171.261 |

For Kimi and GLM, vLLM auto uses FlashKDA. Both Qwen auto columns use the same native FlashInfer provider.

Kimi FlashInfer auto selects cuDNN for this shape. Against the previous FlashInfer baseline, GPU time falls **199.566 → 115.296 µs (42.23%)**; CPU time rises **173.512 → 213.388 µs (22.98%)**. GLM auto stays native. These runs establish no GDN auto GPU gain.

Measured FlashInfer baseline `461037fb` → candidate `669a153d` ([#6259](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6259)); unchanged vLLM caller `29ad8bda`. Frontend **1.31.0**, cuDNN **9.20**, Torch **2.13.0+cu132**; BF16 KDA state and FP32 GDN state. **555 scoped tests passed; 2,880 GPU traces passed audit.**

CPU and GPU were measured separately and must not be added. These are synthetic operator timings, not serving TTFT; small CPU shifts also occur in unchanged controls. [Full B1/B8/B32 prefill/decode results, repeats and raw evidence](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/agopal/kda-vllm-microbench/-/blob/codex/kda-vllm-microbench/measurements/lyris-native-pools-3275022/report.md) (NVIDIA access required).

### Kimi K3 inference — AWS B300, C1 and C8

**8× B300; one 3,600-second sending phase per point.** AWS FlashKDA and FlashInfer auto use the same runtime and node, with BF16 recurrent state, TP8/DCP8, FP4 weights, FP8 KV, DSpark K7 synthetic acceptance 3.84, prefix cache and Mooncake enabled.

| Concurrency | Series | Total tokens/s/chip | Output tokens/s/chip | Median tokens/s/user |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | Published InferenceX [C1](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference/agentic/439932) | 2,025.33 | 15.13 | 236.41 |
| C1 | AWS FlashKDA (BF16 control) | 2,055.41 | 15.52 | 225.82 |
| C1 | AWS FlashInfer auto | 2,159.70 | 16.00 | 259.98 |
| C8 | Published InferenceX [C8](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference/agentic/439935) | 5,180.44 | 40.63 | 127.88 |
| C8 | AWS FlashKDA (BF16 control) | 5,628.14 | 43.05 | 142.79 |
| C8 | AWS FlashInfer auto | 5,790.57 | 43.94 | 169.20 |

**FlashInfer auto change versus the AWS FlashKDA BF16 control:**

| Concurrency | Total tokens/s/chip | Output tokens/s/chip | Median tokens/s/user |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 | +5.07% | +3.08% | +15.13% |
| C8 | +2.89% | +2.06% | +18.50% |

Total throughput includes cached input plus output. Median user rate is **1 / median TPOT**. Rates use the exact raw request window, including completed requests during drain; warmups are excluded. All four AWS points passed validation with **zero request errors or cancellations**. Eight Mooncake lookup errors occurred at startup per point; none occurred during warmup or profiling. JIT, event-loop and cleanup warnings remain in the evidence.

AWS measured vLLM `156420052`, FlashInfer `a7103ae2` (**0.7.2**), frontend **1.31.0**, cuDNN **9.20.0.48**, Torch **2.13.0+cu130**. These measurements predate the current rebase and use a different FlashInfer revision from the microbenchmark; they do not establish that AWS auto selected cuDNN.

**Comparison limits:** FlashKDA supports one intermediate prefill checkpoint block; FlashInfer auto supports zero. Cache settings stayed enabled, but this capability differs. Published InferenceX values are external reference points with runtime, state-dtype and platform differences. Each AWS point is one run; these results do not isolate a kernel-only gain or establish statistical significance.

<details>
<summary>Earlier model evaluation and limits</summary>

The earlier GB200 serving study used vLLM `7c3c1a3f`, FlashInfer `73b63f88`, and frontend `7f85a1f7`. In baseline/auto/cuDNN/cuDNN/auto/baseline order, full GSM8K correct counts were Kimi-K3 **1259/1254/1251/1247/1246/1248 of 1319** and Qwen3-Next **1142/1149/1136/1141/1149/1142 of 1319**. Invalid-answer counts were **1/1/1/1/2/1** and **1/0/0/0/1/0**, respectively. Model accuracy equivalence is not established.

The GLM auto C128 run failed with an RPC timeout and a CUDA error during cleanup. Qwen3.5 cuDNN missed its GSM64 gate (55/64 versus 56 required); those comparisons are incomplete. [Full scores, repeats and failures](https://github.com/Anerudhan/vllm/blob/932292abf35f7948d89255deb60bb844534c7b67/benchmarks/linear_attention/latest_full_gb200_results.md) remain on the source branch. The AWS workload uses synthetic speculative acceptance and does not measure model accuracy.

</details>

## Details

The shared adapter calls FlashInfer's public dispatchers. The cuDNN KDA path uses fused additive Q/K normalization and supports bounded gates with `-5 <= lower_bound < 0`. See `docs/configuration/optimization.md` for usage and limits.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching prefill-selection PR. Related #60470 changes KDA decode; #60050 adds GDN checkpoints; #60105 optimizes native GDN gate conversion and offsets. This PR adds explicit prefill implementation selection and shared KDA integration. It does not include those separate optimizations. AI assistance was used.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

items.title: [Model] Add Laya typed-decision models (Jev /v1/systemone via structured_server)
items.body:
## Overview

Adds [Laya](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya) typed-decision models (`convaiinnovations/laya`, `convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual`) as a `token_classify` pooling model, `LayaForDecision`. It also lets the #57250 structured-decisions server (`/v1/systemone`, Jev's API) front Laya with `--backend laya`.

Laya came up on #57250 as an encoder alternative to DiffusionGemma structured reads. It answers `choice` / `score` / `noul` questions about a state in one forward pass: a ModernBERT/mmBERT encoder plus a small decision head, with no generation.

## Claims

- **Model support.** vLLM serves both public Laya checkpoints (after a one-time layout conversion) and reproduces Laya's own `Agent`. Prompt token ids are identical, every answer matches, and probabilities agree to rounding in fp32.
- **Jev API.** `structured_server.py --backend laya` serves Jev's `/v1/systemone` and the schema-in-system-message `/v1/chat/completions` in front of vLLM's `/pooling`. It supports `depends_on`, `ask_if`, `ask` and `instructions`. `think`, images and raw chat are rejected, because Laya does not generate text.
- **No behavior change for DiffusionGemma.** The two helpers factored out of the diffusion path (`answer_from`, `skip_reason`) leave its output byte-identical.
- **Throughput.** Throughput is on par with Laya's reference runtime. This is not a speedup claim, see Validation.

## Validation

All on B300, rebased on `cb4f016c5d` (model runner v2 active).

**Parity against Laya's reference `Agent`**, using a script in the Laya repo's layout: 4 states (dict, text, conversation list, Hindi) × 6 questions (4-way choice, score, noul, noul with custom labels, binary choice, 12-way choice) per checkpoint.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Prompt token ids vs `laya.common.build_sequence` | identical, 24/24 per checkpoint |
| Chosen answer | same in 48/48 |
| fp32 + `FLEX_ATTENTION`, TF32 off | worst probability gap 1e-4 (the 4-decimal rounding of the answers) |
| bf16 default (`TRITON_ATTN`) | worst gap 0.017 (English), 0.028 (multilingual) |
| Through `structured_server.py --backend laya` | worst gap 0.0054, same answers |

The bf16 gaps are precision noise, not implementation error: Laya runs under autocast with fp32 LayerNorms, while vLLM runs fully in bf16. The fp32/FLEX row isolates this.

**CI test** `tests/models/language/pooling/test_laya.py`:
- It builds a small random checkpoint in the converted layout and compares against a PyTorch port of Laya's `DecisionModel`. One batch mixes question types, option counts (2 to 12, which hits a temperature bucket) and a prompt without markers.
- The public checkpoints need conversion, so CI cannot load them directly.
- Mutation check: a wrong question type, an ignored temperature bucket, a wrong `[CLS]` offset and off-by-one markers each fail the test by 0.036 to 0.62. The real error is 1.5e-3 and the tolerance is 1e-2, so the TF32 attention gap leaves margin on other GPUs.
- The file sits in `tests/models/language/pooling/`, which the Language Models (Extra Pooling) step runs.

```bash
pytest tests/models/language/pooling/test_laya.py   # 1 passed
```

**End to end:**

```bash
python examples/pooling/token_classify/laya/convert_checkpoint.py convaiinnovations/laya ./laya-vllm
vllm serve ./laya-vllm --served-model-name laya
python examples/features/structured_diffusion/structured_server.py --backend laya \
    --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model laya --tokenizer ./laya-vllm
```

- Basic `/v1/systemone`, `ask_if` + `depends_on` staging, the chat-completions schema route and the rejection paths behave as described.
- A prompt with no markers or a bad question type returns an empty output, and the engine stays healthy.
- `laya_offline.py` runs.

**DiffusionGemma path:** the pre- and post-PR `structured_server.decide()` were run with the upstream calls stubbed, across `samples` = 3 / `auto` / 1 and a schema using `ask_if`, `depends_on` and `alone`. The outputs are byte-identical. There is no DiffusionGemma checkpoint on this machine, so the diffusion path was not run end to end.

**Throughput**, English checkpoint, 6 questions per request:

| | decisions/s |
|---|---|
| vLLM, through the HTTP proxy (Python tokenization), concurrency 32 / 128 | 1522 / 1624 |
| Laya `predict_batch`, batch 8 / 32 | 1291 / 1554 |

A single 6-question request takes 14 ms p50. These numbers are from the pre-rebase build.

## Details

**Design.**
- `LayaForDecision` reuses `ModernBertModel` unchanged. On top it adds Laya's question-type embedding and its two pre-norm head layers, the equivalent of `nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(norm_first=True)`, running on `EncoderOnlyAttention`.
- The question type is read from the token after each sequence's `[CLS]` (where `positions == 0`).
- `LayaDecisionPooler` finds each option's `[MASK]` marker from the prompt token ids and scores it. It applies Laya's per-type and per-option-count temperatures, clamped to [0.5, 5] as Laya's `Agent` does, and runs the action head on `[CLS]`.
- Output is one row per option, `[p_option, *p_action]`. `use_activation=false` returns logits.
- The pooler never raises, because it runs inside the engine core: malformed prompts, including profiling dummies, get an empty output.

**Split between model and server**, the same split as DiffusionGemma. The model definition owns the readout: marker detection, question type and calibration. Prompt construction and answer decoding stay client-side, because Laya budgets in tokens (options capped at 48 tokens, the header at `head_max_len`, conversations trimmed from their oldest turn). A chat template cannot express that without changing the token ids. An IO-processor plugin would allow a proxy-free `/v1/systemone`, but plugins currently load only from installed packages, so that is left for a follow-up.

**Checkpoint conversion.** The Hugging Face repos keep `config.json` and the tokenizer in subfolders, so `convert_checkpoint.py` writes a loadable directory:
- the encoder config with `architectures`, a `laya_config` block (head layers, temperatures, `mask_token_id`, question-type token ids) and `dtype` set from Laya's `amp_dtype`;
- the fixed tokenizer;
- the weights, hard-linked.

A repo with a root `config.json` would remove this step and allow a normal model test. The registry entry is `is_available_online=False` until then.

**Compatibility and limitations.**
- **Tensor parallel >1 fails**, from a pre-existing bug. vLLM's `ModernBertAttention` splits the TP-sharded QKV output using the global head count (`modernbert.py:147`), so every ModernBERT model fails at TP>1 on main. This PR does not touch that file. Laya's checkpoints are 322M/421M parameters, so TP is rarely useful. The fix is small (per-rank head counts) and is better as its own PR.
- **Chunked prefill and prefix caching** are off by default for bidirectional pooling models. Forcing them on is unsupported, with the same warning as other encoder-only models. The question-type lookup relies on this.
- **No pipeline parallel.** `SupportsPP` is not implemented.
- **Head layers run eagerly**, outside `torch.compile`. The encoder is still compiled and CUDA-graphed.
- **Laya's `Router`** (English vs multilingual by script) is not ported. Run one server per checkpoint.
- **Saturated action head.** In the English checkpoint `act_probability` is always 1.0. Laya's runtime gives the same.
- **Complexity.** About 268 new lines under `vllm/`, almost all in the self-contained `laya.py`, plus a one-line registry entry. There are no changes to core components.

**Duplicate-work check.** Open PR and issue searches for `laya` and related terms (re-run 2026-09-29) found nothing. Laya appears only in a comment on #57250.

**AI assistance** (Claude) was used for the implementation, validation and this description. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and understanding every changed line.

items.title: [KV Connector][2/N][NIXL] Pipeline-parallel support for PD-disaggregated serving with NIXL connector

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

Adds pipeline-parallel support to the NIXL PD-disaggregated serving path. The
existing NIXL P/D consumer asserted `remote_pp_size == 1` during handshake, and
the producer-side `KVOutputAggregator` rejected `None` `ModelRunnerOutput` from
non-last PP ranks. This PR plumbs producer PP topology end-to-end and re-keys the
consumer-side per-shard state by `(pp_rank, tp_rank)` so a single decoder fans out
handshakes and KV transfers across all producer PP shards.

Supported topology: **heterogeneous PP × TP**, e.g. PP=2 prefiller + TP=2 decoder
on 4 GPUs. The producer's KV is layer-sharded across PP stages while the consumer
is head-sharded across TP ranks, so the connector matches each producer shard's
advertised layers to the local KV regions by name and reshapes on transfer.

Hybrid (Mamba/SSM) producers are explicitly rejected at `register_kv_caches` when
`pp_size > 1` — the per-shard descriptor builder does not yet carry
`mamba_region_*` state. That support is added in a follow-up PR (#43368) to keep
this PR focused.

## Changes

The PP-aware handshake-aggregation and intermediate-PP output foundation landed
separately in #43720 (now merged), so this PR is rebased on `main` and contains
two commits:

| # | Commit | Summary |
|---|--------|---------|
| 1 | `[KVConnector][NIXL] Enable PP-disaggregated KV transfer (single-group, no HMA)` | `NixlConnector` adopts the PP-aware foundation API. `NixlAgentMetadata` carries `pp_rank`, `pp_size`, `start_layer`, `end_layer`, `registered_layer_names`. Per-shard handshake aggregation: `_remote_agents`, `_handshake_futures`, `kv_caches_base_addr`, `dst_xfer_side_handles`, and the per-engine TP mapping are all keyed by `(pp_rank, tp_rank)`; the consumer matches a producer shard's advertised layers to its local KV regions by name and lazily registers a per-shard transfer handle (`src_xfer_handles_by_remote` keyed by `(engine_id, pp_rank, block_size)`); the read path loops over `range(pp_size)` producer stages, each with its own layer range, TP fan-out and block geometry. The scheduler forwards the real `pp_size`; the `remote_pp_size == 1` assertion is dropped. A hybrid-Mamba × PP guard is added at `register_kv_caches`. |
| 2 | `[KVConnector][NIXL] code simplification` | Cleans up commit 1 with **no behavior change**: collapses the `PPLayerMap` dataclass/module into a lightweight `_remote_pp_size: dict[EngineId, int]` "handshake-complete" sentinel (cross-shard partition checks are already covered per-shard in `_validate_remote_agent_handshake`); slims per-shard tracking to `_seen_pp_ranks: dict[EngineId, set[int]]`; drops the redundant `registered_layer_indices` wire field (derived from `registered_layer_names` via `extract_layer_index`); keeps the consumer's own region base addresses in a dedicated `local_kv_caches_base_addr` field; flattens the handshake's PP×TP loops into a single `itertools.product` loop; removes a duplicate `dst_num_blocks` assertion; trims redundant comments. Net −231 LOC. |

Total vs `main`: 12 files, +1,234 / −259 (`worker.py`: +462 / −189).

## Test Plan

### Unit + integration
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_transfer_topology_sharded.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_consumer_shard_refactor.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_handshake_aggregation.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_pp_metadata.py
```

### End-to-end correctness (GSM8K)

Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct on a 4×GB200 node, full GSM8K (1319 problems, 5-shot, chat
template), through the toy proxy at `127.0.0.1:8000`. Two stacks are compared: the
heterogeneous **PP=2 prefiller (GPUs 0,1) + TP=2 decoder (GPUs 2,3)** path this PR
adds, and the existing **TP=2 prefiller + TP=2 decoder** PD baseline.

Prefiller (PP=2):
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 \
  vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --port 8100 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer"}'
```
Decoder (TP=2):
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 \
  vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --port 8200 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}'
```
Proxy + eval:
```bash
python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py \
  --port 8000 --prefiller-hosts 127.0.0.1 --prefiller-ports 8100 \
  --decoder-hosts 127.0.0.1 --decoder-ports 8200

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template
```

> `--enforce-eager` sidesteps an unrelated flashinfer `allreduce_fusion` API drift
> on the TP>1 decode path on current `main`; it is not required by the connector.

## Test Result

**Unit + integration:** 118 passed / 2 skipped across the NIXL unit + integration
suites listed above.

**End-to-end GSM8K (full 1319, 5-shot, chat):**

| Stack | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|-------|------------------|--------------|
| PP=2 prefill → TP=2 decode (this PR) | **0.9424** ±0.0064 | 0.8916 ±0.0086 |
| TP=2 prefill → TP=2 decode (baseline) | 0.9386 ±0.0066 | 0.8893 ±0.0086 |

The heterogeneous PP×TP path matches the non-PP PD baseline within eval noise
(Δ 0.0038 ≪ combined stderr), confirming the layer-sharded → head-sharded KV
transfer is correct and the PP path does not regress the existing PD path.

**Throughput (representative; PP=2 prefill + TP=2 decode, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct,
4×GB200, input=8192 / output=128 / concurrency=1, 10 prompts):**

```
================= Serving Benchmark Result =================
Successful requests:                     10
Failed requests:                         0
Maximum request concurrency:             1
Benchmark duration (s):                  84.07
Total input tokens:                      81910
Total generated tokens:                  1280
Request throughput (req/s):              0.12
Output token throughput (tok/s):         15.22
Total token throughput (tok/s):          989.48
Mean TTFT (ms):                          6619.96
Mean TPOT (ms):                          14.07
Mean E2EL (ms):                          8406.96
============================================================
```
10/10 requests succeeded; NIXL KV transfers fanned out from the PP0/PP1 producer
shards into the TP-sharded decoder for every request.

**Pre-PR**, the same heterogeneous setup failed at `_nixl_handshake`'s
`remote_pp_size == 1` assertion; post-PR the consumer fans out per-shard
handshakes successfully (results above).

## Why this is not a duplicate

Re-checked vLLM open PRs/issues for `pipeline parallel disaggregated NIXL`, `PP
NIXL connector`, `consumer per-shard`, and related variants. No open PR covers the
heterogeneous PP × TP consumer per-shard refactor implemented here. The
PP-aware-foundation portion landed in #43720; HMA-under-PP support is a separate
follow-up (#43368), so each PR maps to a single concern.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitting human
reviewed every changed line, ran every test referenced above, and is responsible
for defending the change end-to-end.

items.title: [Model] Add HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-14B reasoning and tool parsers
items.body:
## Summary
Adds built-in reasoning and tool parsers for `naver-hyperclovax/HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-14B`,
registered as `hyperclovax_seed_think_14b` for both `--reasoning-parser` and
`--tool-call-parser`:

```bash
vllm serve naver-hyperclovax/HyperCLOVAX-SEED-Think-14B \
  --reasoning-parser hyperclovax_seed_think_14b \
  --tool-call-parser hyperclovax_seed_think_14b \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

The model emits tool calls as `<|im_start|>assistant -> tool/function_call\n[{...}]` and
reasoning after a `/think` prompt; this parser turns that into structured `reasoning_content`
and `tool_calls`. (It is a separate parser from the 32B variant, whose chat template and
tool-call format differ.)

## Attribution & test versions
The parser logic is adapted from the official HyperCLOVA X vLLM plugin
(https://github.com/NAVER-Cloud-HyperCLOVA-X/hcx-vllm-plugin) — the plugin linked from the
HuggingFace model card — and ported to vLLM's built-in conventions (single self-contained
module, lazy registration, modernized imports).

The reference plugin's last tool-parser commit is ~10 months old, so to preserve its import
compatibility it is tested on **`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.9.2`**, while this PR (modernized imports)
is tested on **`v0.21.0`**.

## The problem and the fix (`tool_choice="required"`)
The reference plugin's reasoning-end boundary detection (`is_reasoning_end` /
`extract_content_ids`) is not tuned for the structured-output path, so vLLM's grammar engages
at the wrong token for `tool_choice="required"`. This PR tightens that boundary so the grammar
applies from the correct token.

**Test matrix — 54 cases** (each axis varied independently):

| group | axes | count |
|--|--|--|
| tool | `tool_choice` {auto, required} × `stream` {true, false} × `force_reasoning` {none, true, false} × `skip_reasoning` {none, true, false} | 2×2×3×3 = **36** |
| reasoner | `force_reasoning` {none, true, false} × `skip_reasoning` {none, true, false} × `stream` {true, false} | 3×3×2 = **18** |
| **total** | | **54** |

Each matrix was run **with and without** the model card's recommended tool-use system prompt:

| parser (vLLM version) × system prompt | required (ok/18) | auto tool_calls (/18) | reasoner (/18) | errors |
|--|--|--|--|--|
| reference (v0.9.2) + official prompt | **0/18** | 18/18 | 18/18 | 3× HTTP 400 |
| **this PR** (v0.21.0) + official prompt | **18/18** | 18/18 | 18/18 | 0 |
| **this PR** (v0.21.0) + no prompt | **18/18** | 0/18 | 18/18 | 0 |
| reference (v0.9.2) + no prompt | **0/18** | 0/18 | 18/18 | 4× HTTP 400 |

Two independent axes:
- **`required` is decided by the parser (system-prompt-independent).** The reference plugin
  fails 18/18 regardless of prompt — `finish_reason=stop` instead of `tool_calls`, HTTP 400
  with `force_reasoning`, or no tool call when streaming. This PR passes **18/18 regardless**.
- **`auto` is decided by the system prompt (parser-independent).** With the recommended
  tool-use prompt both reach 18/18; without it both reach 0/18 (see model-format limitation
  below).
- **`reasoner` is correct in all four conditions.**

## Model-format limitation under `auto` (not a parser bug)
Without the model card's recommended tool-use system prompt, the model follows the prompt
format it was trained on less reliably, and `tool_choice="auto"` produces two off-spec cases.
Ideal output (per the chat template):

```text
<|im_start|>assistant -> tool/function_call
[{"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Seoul", "unit": "celsius"}}]<|im_end|>
```

Observed off-spec cases (`auto`, empty system prompt, input `"서울 날씨 알려줘."` + a
`get_current_weather` tool; `temperature=0, seed=42`):

```text
# Case 1 — real function name instead of "function_call", bare object instead of array.
#          (The tool intent is present, just off-format.)
-> tool/get_current_weather
{"location": "Seoul", "unit": "celsius"}

# Case 2 — plain text, no tool call at all. (The model chose not to call a tool.)
현재 서울의 날씨 정보를 가져올 수 없습니다. 하지만, 아래 링크를 통해 ...
```

- Under **`tool_choice="required"`** the boundary fix lets vLLM's grammar force the canonical
  `[{...}]` form, so **both cases come out as valid tool calls** (the 18/18 above).
- Under **`auto`** there is no grammar, so neither is recovered: Case 1 is off-format and
  Case 2 has no tool intent to recover from. The parser returns the text as `content` rather
  than fabricating a call.

This is a **model-format limitation** (the model adheres to a specific system-prompt format),
not a parser defect: supplying the recommended tool-use system prompt makes `auto` produce
valid calls too (18/18 in the matrix). What the parser *does* add on top of the required-path
fix is robust handling of canonical-format variants (bare-array hand-off, `arguments`↔
`parameters`, dash-prefixed arrays, multiple calls).

## Update — non-streaming `<|im_end|>` boundary fix (review feedback)

Addressing @Incheonkirin's review
(https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44171#issuecomment-4672111272): in the
non-streaming path a literal `<|im_end|>` inside a JSON **string argument** was taken as
the tool-call boundary (text search via `find("<|im_end|>")` / the regex), truncating the
JSON so `json.loads` failed and the call was silently dropped (`tools_called=False`).

- The tool-call array is now located by JSON structure with `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode`
  (respects JSON string escaping) instead of cutting at the literal token.
- Applied to **both** the tool parser (`extract_tool_calls`) and the reasoning parser
  (`_strip_tool_end_tokens` / `extract_reasoning`): in the non-streaming auto+reasoning path
  the reasoning parser strips the boundary before the tool parser receives the payload, so
  both need the structure-aware approach.
- `raw_decode` accepts trailing data after `]` (the terminator token) where the previous
  slicing rejected it; kept as-is since the trailing content is harmless here.

This is the originating PR for these parsers; the change above addresses review feedback on
this same PR (not a separate/duplicate change).

## Tests run
**Unit (mock tokenizer, no GPU) — 29/29 passed** (26 existing + 3 new regression cases for a literal `<|im_end|>` inside an argument)
```bash
python -m pytest tests/reasoning/test_hyperclovax_seed_think_14b_reasoning_parser.py \
                 tests/tool_parsers/test_hyperclovax_seed_think_14b_tool_parser.py -v
```
Covers the 9-combination `force_reasoning × skip_reasoning` matrix, reasoning↔content boundary
split, streaming, `is_reasoning_end` boundary detection, and the tool-call forms above, in both
non-streaming and streaming paths.

**End-to-end:** the 54-case matrix above (14B served with the built-in parser).
**Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

## AI assistance
This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every
changed line and ran the tests above.

## Naming note
Uses the `_14b` suffix to distinguish it from the 32B variant, whose chat template and
tool-call format differ. Happy to rename per maintainer preference.

items.title: [Perf][Gemma4][Multimodal] Fuse Gemma4Unified 2D posemb and batch image/video embedder
items.body:
## Overview This pull request optimizes the vision and multimodal input processing pipeline of `Gemma4Unified` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`, used by `google/gemma-4-12B-it`) via two key performance and architectural enhancements: 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Factorized Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: Replaces the sequential, un-fused PyTorch loop over coordinate axes and position indices with a single clean, vectorized PyTorch implementation using contiguous 1D `F.embedding` lookups on `self.pos_embedding.view(-1, embed_dim)`, in-place `.add_` accumulation, and masked fill, cleanly preserving `positions_xy != -1` coordinate masking with 100% bit-exact numerical parity without requiring Triton or custom C++/CUDA kernels. 2. **Memory-Bounded Chunking & Cross-Request Image & Multi-Frame Video Batching**: Vectorizes `_process_image_input` (both 3D `torch.Tensor` and `list[torch.Tensor]`) and `_process_video_input` across all prompt requests and video frames into unified 2D batch GEMM projections (`self.patch_dense` and `self.embed_vision`), eliminating per-request and per-frame Python iteration overhead. Memory usage is safely bounded via `_vision_chunk` which dynamically mirrors `_encoder_chunk` logic and bounds peak memory per chunk based on available accelerator memory (short-circuiting memory queries when batch size <= 1, and guarded with `gpu_sync_allowed()`). **Vectorized Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: **1.25x – 1.38x speedup** (`0.310 ms -> 0.248 ms` at 280 tokens; `0.325 ms -> 0.236 ms` at 2240 tokens) with **100.0% bit-exact parity**. - **Batched Image Input Processing (`_process_image_input`)**: - Technical Details ### Root Cause Analysis In `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`): 1. **Un-vectorized 2D Position Embedding Kernel**: `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb` previously computed factorized 2D sinusoidal position embeddings using separate PyTorch operations: slicing coordinate channels, executing multiple 3D tensor indexing lookups (`self.pos_embedding[clamped_pos[..., 0], 0, :]`), masking invalid patch positions where `positions_xy != -1`, and concatenating/normalizing. On modern GPUs, dispatching multiple small kernels over 280-2240 visual tokens caused excessive kernel launch latency (~0.31 ms), bounding vision preprocessing throughput. 2. **Sequential Un-batched Multimodal Inputs**: In `_process_image_input`, when multiple images were passed (either as a 3D tensor or a list of tensors across requests in continuous batching), each image was processed individually through `self.vision_embedder` and `self.embed_vision` via an inline `for pv, pp in zip(pixel_values, pixel_position_ids)` loop. Similarly, `_process_video_input` iterated over each video and each frame sequentially in Python. For an 8-frame video, this dispatched 8 independent vision embedder projections and 8 `ColumnParallelLinear` multimodal projections, incurring significant CPU launch overhead and leaving GPU SMs underutilized. ### Implementation Details 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: - Replaces multi-step 3D tensor slicing with a single contiguous 1D embedding lookup using `F.embedding`. - Flattens `self.pos_embedding` from `[max_size, 2, embed_dim]` to `[max_size * 2, embed_dim]` via `.view(-1, embed_dim)`. - Computes flat indices `x_flat = pos_x * 2` and `y_flat = pos_y * 2 + 1`, clamping `-1` padding values before lookup. - Computes `out = F.embedding(x_flat, flat_weights)` and performs an in-place accumulation `out.add_(F.embedding(y_flat, flat_weights))`. - Applies `.masked_fill_(~valid_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)` in-place where `positions_xy == -1`, producing exact zero padding and preserving 100% bit-exact parity without Triton or custom kernel dependencies. 2. **Memory-Bounded Dynamic Chunking (`_vision_chunk` and `_embed_vision_patches`)**: - Mirrors the proven `_encoder_chunk` mechanism to dynamically split large image/video batches based on available accelerator memory budget, avoiding OOMs on large multimodal prompts. - Short-circuits when `total_items <= 1` (a single image or video), directly passing inputs through without executing the `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()` syscall. - Wraps accelerator memory queries with `with gpu_sync_allowed():` context guards to respect vLLM async execution and CUDA graph capture invariants. 3. **Unified Batched Multimodal Projections**: - `_process_image_input`: - When receiving a 3D `torch.Tensor` of shape `[N, S, D]` (batched images), it passes the tensor directly through `self._embed_vision_patches` in one pass, flattens all patches across images to `[N * S, D_in]`, executes a single batched GEMM projection through `self.embed_vision`, and unbinds into per-image feature chunks. - When receiving a `list[torch.Tensor]` of variable-length images, it flattens each image's patch tokens, tracks slice lengths, concatenates into a unified 2D batch `[total_patches, D]`, runs a single `self.embed_vision` projection, and splits back into per-image tensors using `torch.split`. - `_process_video_input`: - Embeds all frames of all videos in a single unified tensor pass through `self._embed_vision_patches` and `self.embed_vision`, splitting features by `video_frame_counts`. ### Tradeoffs & Encapsulation - **Zero Non-Gemma Regressions**: All modifications are strictly encapsulated within `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. Standard Gemma 4 models (`E2B`, `E4B`, `26B-A4B`, `31B`) and text-only generation paths are completely untouched. - **Pure PyTorch Simplicity & Portability**: Completely eliminates the need for Triton or hardware-specific kernels, ensuring immediate zero-overhead support across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD ROCm, TPUs, and CPUs. - **Bit-Exact Numerical Fidelity**: Position embedding outputs are 100.0% bit-exact to PyTorch reference implementations. Full image and video embeddings retain 100.0% bit-exact parity at low batch sizes and > 0.99999 cosine similarity across large batches. ### Model & Workload Applicability Matrix | Model / Workload | Direct / Transitive / N/A | Supported Architecture | Technical Justification | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | | `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | Direct Optimization | Gemma4Unified (Encoder-free Vision) | Uses `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. | | `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. items.title: [Perf][EPLB][DSv4] Add a symm_mem weight-migration backend and fuse MegaMoE replica mapping
items.body:
## Overview

This PR makes EPLB cheaper for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, running DP attention with EP MegaMoE on multi-node NVLink. It does three things:

- adds an opt-in `symm_mem` weight-migration backend;
- fuses EPLB's logical→physical replica mapping and expert-load recording into the DeepGEMM MegaMoE staging kernels;
- takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path.

Not a duplicate. No open or merged PR adds a symmetric-memory EPLB backend or fuses the MegaMoE mapping. #61176 and #61839 enable EPLB for the ROCm AITER MegaMoE backend. Related: #61767 (`cpu_all_reduce_`, reused here), #57549, #56716, #61643.

## Claims

- EPLB raises decode throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 NVL72 by +3.7% at DEP32 with 72 req/rank and +7.7% at DEP32 with 128 req/rank. At DEP16 the step is about 3% shorter, but the throughput gain is within run-to-run noise.
- `symm_mem`: senders push expert rows into the receiver's `expert_buffer`, which is allocated in CUDA symmetric memory. There is no staging buffer, and it needs no memory beyond `expert_buffer`. Cross-node peer copies run at about 800 GB/s, against about 88 GB/s for NIXL, and a 40-layer rearrangement transfers in 0.3–0.6 s at DEP32.
- MegaMoE layers no longer launch a separate EPLB mapping kernel, which saves 5–6 µs per layer. The replica choice is shared with the router through one Triton helper, so physical ids and load counts match `eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` exactly.
- Async EPLB no longer adds a GPU→host sync to the decode loop. It also raises on every rank when the worker fails on any rank, instead of stalling.

## Validation

Hardware: GB200 NVL72, 4 GPUs per node.

Serving setup: DSpark with 5 draft tokens, MRV2, FULL CUDA graphs, async scheduling.

EPLB setup: `{"num_redundant_experts": <DP>, "window_size": 1000, "step_interval": 3000, "use_async": true, "communicator": "symm_mem"}`, i.e. one redundant expert per rank.

Workload: decode only, coding-agent prompts with mean ISL ≈ 85k (prefix-cached), 16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, and requests pinned evenly to DP ranks. Throughput is the output rate over the window in which every request is decoding.

Off and on arms ran interleaved (ABAB) on the same nodes. These runs used a branch of nightly fe4df3df (2026-10-12) with this change set and #61767, before the rebase and without the second commit.

| Config | EPLB off (tok/s) | EPLB on (tok/s) | Δ | Welch t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16, 72 req/rank | 223.6k ± 2.0k (n=4) | 228.1k ± 4.2k (n=4) | +2.0% | 2.0 (not resolved) |
| DEP32, 72 req/rank | 419.5k ± 1.3k (n=4) | 435.1k ± 5.8k (n=4) | +3.7% | 5.3 |
| DEP32, 128 req/rank | 500.7k ± 5.1k (n=3) | 539.4k ± 9.7k (n=3) | +7.7% | 6.1 |

- DEP16 step time, p50 of 2000-step windows at full batch, same build: 24.34 / 24.28 ms off vs 23.61 / 23.25 ms on.
- At DEP32 with 128 req/rank, one pass per arm is excluded. A host stall unrelated to EPLB cut that pass by 13–34%.

Per-step breakdown, DEP32 with 128 req/rank:

| | EPLB off | EPLB on |
|---|---|---|
| Step time (CUDA events, unprofiled) | 38.8 ms | 36.5 ms |
| GPU idle at the step boundary | 0.27 ms | 0.27 ms |
| Main-model MegaMoE (5 s CUDA profile) | 18.1 ms | 13.4 ms |
| All other kernels (same profile) | 21.5 ms | 21.2 ms |

The GPU never waits on the host, so the MegaMoE saving turns into step time. MegaMoE is about 40% of the step, which caps the end-to-end gain.

Microbenchmarks (GB200):

- **Fused EPLB staging**, one MoE layer, hidden 5120, top-k 6, 384 logical experts. Each arm is timed as a CUDA graph replay, median of 200. Outputs, ids and load counts match main bit for bit in every case.

  | Format | Tokens | Physical experts | main: `torch.where` + map kernel + staging | Fused | Saved |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MXFP8 | 432 | 400 | 9.4 µs | 4.2 µs | 5.1 µs |
  | MXFP8 | 768 | 416 | 11.0 µs | 4.7 µs | 6.3 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 432 | 400 | 49.5 µs | 44.0 µs | 5.5 µs |
  | NVFP4 | 768 | 416 | 49.1 µs | 43.8 µs | 5.3 µs |

  That is about 0.2 ms per decode step across 40 MoE layers.
- **Weight-migration bandwidth**, 2 nodes, one MegaMoE layer of 25 experts (470 MB):

  | Path | Bandwidth |
  |---|---|
  | `symm_mem` peer copies, intra- or cross-node over multi-node NVLink | ~808 GB/s (bulk), ~294 GB/s (100 per-tensor copies) |
  | NIXL, cross-node | ~88 GB/s (UCX picks RoCE, not multi-node NVLink) |
  | NIXL, cross-node, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp` | ~0.12 GB/s (TCP) |

- **MegaMoE kernel time under serving load**, DEP16 with 72 req/rank, layers 2–40: p50 per call drops 12.6–14.0% across three profiled runs (222→194 µs). Layer 1 is excluded because it absorbs cross-rank arrival skew.

Tests on this branch, one GB200 node with 4 GPUs. They ran before the rebase onto 64175d3827; the 5 newer commits on main touch none of these files.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py` (incl. `test_prepare_megamoe_eplb_matches_router_under_graph_replay`) | 110 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k eplb` | 18 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py` | 35 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU) |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k nixl`, NIXL installed | 7 passed |
| `tests/distributed/test_eplb_utils.py`, `test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py` | 6 passed, 28 passed |
| `tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` | 13 passed, 7 passed |

GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (one node):
- Setup: 5-shot, 1319 questions, temperature 0, `num_redundant_experts=16`, `window_size=100`, `step_interval=300`. Every arm rearranged all 40 layers four times during the eval.
- Command: `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`

| Arm | Accuracy (2 passes) | 40-layer rearrangement |
|---|---|---|
| EPLB off | 0.898, 0.901 | — |
| `symm_mem` | 0.897, 0.895 | 2.9–3.3 s |
| `symm_mem`, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 0.889, 0.883 | 2.9–3.3 s, no sync error |
| `nixl` | 0.892, 0.886 | 2.7–3.2 s |

The EPLB-off and `nixl` arms ran on the commit before the final cleanup, which does not touch either path. Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate; `symm_mem`'s advantage is across nodes over multi-node NVLink.

## Details

**`symm_mem` backend**
- The receive buffer is one symmetric `uint8` buffer per EP group, set up with a single rendezvous and carved into per-tensor views. The backend checks the NVLink/MNNVL domain before allocating.
- Senders and receivers derive each receive row from the global placement with the same helper, so `add_recv` is a no-op. Push backends get every rank's rows through a new `recv_rows` argument to `set_transfer_context`. This argument is optional and other backends ignore it.
- Each `execute()` runs two CPU barriers. GPU spin barriers can deadlock against MegaMoE's cooperative launches.
- Rejected with elastic EP. The buffer lives outside the caching allocator, so sleep mode does not free it.

**Fused mapping**: `fused_moe/eplb_triton.py` holds the replica hash, map lookup and gated load count. The MXFP8/BF16 and NVFP4 staging kernels call it, and so does the router kernel. Routed-experts capture still sees logical ids.

**Async EPLB**
- Per-layer maps are committed with pinned non-blocking copies, and the worker thread fences `expert_buffer` reuse.
- Balancedness stats are read back non-blocking and logged in order once they land.
- `should_record_tensor` is rewritten only when its value flips.
- The per-step "all ranks ready" check runs over `cpu_all_reduce_`. A gloo ring all-reduce costs several ms per step at DP16/DP32.

**Also**
- `logical_to_physical_map` is sized to R+1 slots unless elastic EP is on.
- `compute_logical_maps` is vectorized.
- DeepSeek V4.1 decoder-replay padding and dummy rows are marked as padding, which complements #61643.

**CI**: the `symm_mem` execution tests need NVLink peers. They are added to the optional 8×H100 "Distributed DP + EP" job; the 4×L4 EPLB job skips them. The MegaMoE parity test needs SM100.

**Limitations**
- In mixed prefill/decode serving, per-rank prefill imbalance bounds the step. There, EPLB mostly lowers tail TTFT rather than raising throughput.
- Likely rebase overlap with #61786, #59168 and #41141. Offline placements without elastic EP (#41141) could exceed R+1 replicas.

---

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Fused DSA indexer Top-k kernel (LiteTopk)
items.body:
## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

**At 1M-token prefill, LiteTopK accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash by 1.29× and 1.08×, respectively. LiteDSA increases the end-to-end speedups to 1.40× and 1.25×, with no accuracy loss.**

Thanks to my collaborators Jianyang Gao ([@gaoj0017](https://github.com/gaoj0017)) from ETH Zurich, Peiqi Yin ([@yinpeiqi](https://github.com/yinpeiqi)) from CUHK, and Jiangneng Li ([@gravesprite](https://github.com/gravesprite)) from NTU.

### Motivation

DSA models such as **DeepSeek-V3.2/DeepSeek-V4**, **GLM-4.6/GLM-5.2**, and **LongCat-2.0** use a sparse-attention indexer during prefill. The current indexer computes an FP8 MQA score for every query/KV pair, materializes a `[num_q, seq_len]` matrix in HBM, and then runs a per-row TopK:

```python
logits = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(...)        # materializes [num_q, seq_len] in HBM
ops.top_k_per_row_prefill(logits, ...)  # TopK over the materialized matrix
```

At 256K–1M context, this transient matrix is both large and expensive to write and read. After the indexer, the sparse-attention path launches many narrow per-token attention GEMMs. Neighboring queries usually select substantially overlapping KV positions, so those kernels repeatedly load and process much of the same KV data; at high tensor-parallel degrees, padding a small number of local heads to the kernel tile shape also wastes tensor-core work.

### LiteTopK: fused indexer scoring and TopK

LiteTopK avoids storing the score matrix:

1. Score KV tiles with FP8 MQA using tcgen05 UMMA.
2. Maintain an online **bucketed gate** with 256 histogram buckets and a self-calibrating threshold, discarding unlikely positions as scores are produced.
3. Run a compact TopK over the surviving candidates.

The candidate workspace is bounded independently of `seq_len`, replacing the dense `O(num_q × seq_len)` logits allocation and its extra HBM pass.

### LiteDSA: grouped masked sparse attention

LiteDSA targets the attention stage after TopK. If a rank owns `H` query heads, it groups `G = 128 / H` adjacent query tokens and packs their `G × H` real query/head rows into one 128-row tensor-core tile. For example, GLM-5.2 TP8 packs 16 neighboring tokens per attention call. Instead of running `G` small sparse GEMMs, LiteDSA performs one larger GEMM over the union of their selected KV positions.

The grouped computation remains query-exact:

1. **Union and KV reuse.** A GPU bitmap kernel deduplicates the group's TopK lists, emits the union in ascending order, and fuses logical-to-physical block-table conversion. Neighboring queries exhibit strong causal locality; the GLM path observes roughly 6–7× KV deduplication.
2. **Per-query masking.** A query-major membership bitmask records which union entries belong to each original query. The masked FP8 attention kernel applies this mask before softmax, so every query attends to exactly its original TopK set.
3. **Lower orchestration overhead.** Union, membership, and output buffers are persistent overwrite-write buffers. The union plan is version-cached and reused across layers that share the same indexer output, avoiding repeated allocation, clearing, and reconstruction.

DeepSeek-V4's C128A path uses the same packing principle with a structure-aware specialization. At TP8, 16 tokens × 8 real heads fill one 128-row tile instead of padding each token from 8 to 64 heads. Its compressed-prefix plus sliding-window structure is represented by exact per-query ranges over the group union; the ranges are derived directly from positions, cached per chunk, and avoid materializing the `[num_tokens, topk + window]` combined-index matrix. The measured union size is only 1.002× that of a single token.

In both paths, each union KV entry is loaded once for the group rather than repeatedly for every neighboring query. Unsupported shapes, CUDA Graph capture, non-SM100 devices, and other ineligible configurations transparently fall back to the existing attention path.

### Configuration

```bash
# LiteTopK indexer + existing sparse attention
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litetopk vllm serve <dsa-model> ...

# LiteTopK indexer + LiteDSA grouped sparse attention (supported FP8 sparse MLA path)
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litedsa vllm serve <dsa-model> ...

# DeepSeek-V4 C128A head-packed attention specialization
VLLM_DSV4_PACKED_ATTN=1 vllm serve <deepseek-v4-model> ...
```

## 🧪 Test Plan

> The kernel and end-to-end checks require an SM100 (B200) build and a DSA model.

```bash
# Build for SM100
uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto

# LiteDSA orchestration, buffer-lifetime, and DeepSeek-V4 packed-path tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/model_executor/layers/test_litedsa.py \
    tests/model_executor/layers/test_dsv4_packed_attn.py

# End-to-end long-context parity and performance
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litetopk \
    vllm serve <dsa-model> --max-model-len ...
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litedsa \
    vllm serve <dsa-model> --max-model-len ...

# Model evaluation for output parity
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=<dsa-model>,...  # compare raw/litetopk/litedsa
```

## ✅ Test Results

### LiteTopK kernel-level validation

Hardware: NVIDIA B200 (SM100). Inputs: real GLM-5.2 indexer tensors, `Q=8192`, `top_k=2048`.

The dense FP32 logits buffer consumes **8 GiB at 256K, 16 GiB at 512K, 24 GiB at 768K, and 32 GiB at 1M**. LiteTopK removes this allocation.

| KV length | Dense (ms) | LiteTopK (ms) | Paired speedup median | Recall median |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 262,144 | 13.0469 | 10.6117 | 1.2266× | 99.9977% |
| 524,288 | 25.8997 | 20.4716 | 1.2652× | 99.9980% |
| 786,432 | 39.2471 | 30.0235 | 1.3084× | 99.9978% |
| 1,048,576 | 51.8106 | 40.1796 | 1.2929× | 99.9978% |

Recall rounds to **100.00%** at two decimal places across the tested settings.

### LiteDSA kernel-level validation

On captured DeepSeek-V4 C128A production data, head packing reduces sparse-attention kernel time from **6.565 ms to 0.839 ms (7.83×)**. Validation reports LSE max absolute error of `3e-6` and output relative error of `0.0025`.

### End-to-end 1M-token prefill

| Model | Input tokens | Dense (s) | LiteTopK (s) | LiteTopK speedup | LiteDSA (s) | LiteDSA speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GLM-5.2 TP8+EP8 | 1M | 152.89 | 118.66 | 1.29× | 109.14 | 1.40× |
| DeepSeek-V4 TP4+EP | 1M | 60.00 | 55.7 | 1.08× | 48.1 | 1.25× |

## Author

Ziqi Yin, Nanyang Technological University

items.title: refactor(envs): migrate vllm/envs.py to pydantic-settings
items.body:
## Summary

Refactors `vllm/envs.py` to use `pydantic-settings`, addressing [RFC #31249](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/31249).

Each env var now has a **single declaration** — type, default, description, and (where relevant) alias or validator — on a domain-specific `BaseSettings` sub-class. The public `vllm.envs.VLLM_X` attribute API is preserved. Anything derived from env vars (the docs page, `torch.compile` cache keys) is generated from those field declarations instead of hand-maintained parallel lists, so it cannot drift.

## Architecture

- Env vars are grouped into domain-specific `BaseSettings` sub-classes (build, paths, server, logging, distributed, compilation, media, CPU, ROCm, TPU/XPU, FlashInfer, quant, connector, usage), composed into one root `Settings`.
- `env_prefix="VLLM_"` covers the majority of fields. Non-`VLLM_` vars (`MAX_JOBS`, `S3_*`, `LOCAL_RANK`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `NO_COLOR`, …) use explicit `alias=`.
- Cross-cutting defaults (e.g. `VLLM_DP_RANK_LOCAL` → `VLLM_DP_RANK`, torch-version-dependent AOT flags, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` ↔ `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_LOCATION`) live in a root `@model_validator(mode="after")`. `VLLM_DO_NOT_TRACK` / `DO_NOT_TRACK` fallback uses `AliasChoices`.
- Hand-rolled coercion helpers (`maybe_convert_int`, `env_with_choices`, `env_list_with_choices`, `get_env_or_set_default`, `use_aot_compile`, …) are deleted in favor of pydantic's native parsing, `Literal`, and validators.
- `environment_variables` and `maybe_convert_bool` are kept as back-compat shims for external callers (`vllm/collect_env.py`, `vllm/ray/ray_env.py`, `tests/ci_envs.py`, …).

The file is intentionally *larger* than before: each field now carries its type, default, and full prose description inline (previously split across a `TYPE_CHECKING` block and a runtime `environment_variables` dict). One declaration site per var is the goal, and it also feeds the docs generator.

## Design decisions

**Docs generated from the model.** `docs/mkdocs/plugins/gen_env_vars.py` walks `Settings.model_fields` at build time and writes `docs/configuration/env_vars.md` (one anchored H3 per env var, grouped by sub-model). Adding or editing a var's `Field(description=...)` updates the docs automatically — no separate edit. `mkdocs.yaml` registers the `gen-files` plugin; `requirements/docs.in` adds `pydantic-settings`.

**Declarative `torch.compile` cache factors.** `compile_factors()` returns the env vars hashed into `torch.compile` cache keys. This was previously *all known vars minus a hand-maintained `ignored_factors` literal* — a second source of truth edited on nearly every merge, which had already drifted (a dead entry with no backing field). It is now a **per-field property**: a var is a compile factor by default, and non-factors carry `json_schema_extra={"compile_factor": False}` on their `Field`. `compile_factors()` derives the exclude-set from the field definitions at runtime, so it cannot drift.

The **opt-out polarity** is deliberate: a forgotten marker leaves a var *in* the factor set (over-hashing → at most a harmless extra cache miss), never silently drops a real factor (which could serve a stale compiled artifact). This is a representation-only change — the set of real compile factors is unchanged apart from dropping the dead entry.

## Behavior changes (all non-breaking)

1. **Bool coercion widened.** Pydantic accepts `yes/no/on/off` in addition to `1/0/true/false` — a superset of the previous accept set.
2. **`VLLM_MM_HASHER_ALGORITHM` and `VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION` are coerced to lower-case.** No-op for `MM_HASHER` (its consumer already `.lower()`s). For `FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION` it's a small fix: `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision()` is case-sensitive and silently no-ops on upper-case input, so `=HIGH` was previously ignored by torch.
3. **`TYPE_CHECKING`-vs-runtime drift fixed.** A few vars had the type-checker view disagreeing with the runtime default (e.g. `VLLM_DP_MASTER_IP` annotated `""` but defaulting to `"127.0.0.1"`). Runtime values are preserved exactly.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_envs.py tests/test_envs_pydantic.py tests/docs/test_env_vars_gen.py` — passing. Covers `VLLM_X` attribute parity, alias/validator/fallback behavior, `compile_factors()` determinism and relocation invariance, the declarative compile-factor drift guard, and the docs-generator output.
- [x] The compile-factor migration was verified exact during development (runtime-derived exclude-set asserted equal to the frozen pre-refactor literal minus the dead entry); that one-time gate was retired for a permanent drift guard.
- [x] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` (matching CI deps) clean across changed files.
- [x] `mkdocs build` completes; the env-vars page renders one anchored section per var.

To run on CI / Linux + CUDA:

- [ ] Smoke: `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m` starts.
- [ ] `mkdocs build --strict` on readthedocs.

## Local docs build

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-docs
uv pip install --python .venv-docs/bin/python --no-cache-dir -r requirements/docs.txt
.venv-docs/bin/mkdocs serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/configuration/env_vars/
```
